description.narrative: The PDO is to improve the effectiveness and coordination of selected public programs to alleviate constraints to competitiveness and job creation, including investment and export promotion, innovation, active labor market programs and labor intermediation.

The objective of the Competitiveness and Jobs Project for Serbia is to improve the effectiveness and coordination of selected public programs to alleviate constraints to competitiveness and job creation, including investment and export promotion, innovation, active labor market programs, labor intermediation, and activation of social assistance beneficiaries. There are three components to the project, the first component being policy planning, monitoring, and coordination. This component supports the implementation of the Borrower's program for policy planning, monitoring, and coordination (PPMC) through developing and piloting an inter-ministerial PPMC system in support of competitiveness and jobs reforms (see DLI 1). This will also include development of individual planning and monitoring frameworks at the ministry level (to feed into the inter-ministerial PPMC system), and the piloting of the PPMC system, including through semi-annual progress reports and annual performance review reports with inputs from each participating ministry. The second component is the investment and export promotion. This component supports implementation of the Borrower's program for investment and export promotion through (see DLI 2): developing and adopting a strategic framework and overall action plan for investment and export promotion, including restructuring the MoE investment and export promotion agencies, and improving the Borrower's investment and export promotion programs and services. Finally, the third component is the innovation. This component supports of implementation of the Borrower's program for innovation through: supporting the operations of the innovation fund and its matching grants program; supporting the Technology Transfer Facility (TTF) service lines at the innovation fund; and undertaking strategic planning for institutional reform of the public research and development sector.

title.narrative: Technology transfer: IF TTF service lines deployed [see DLI 4]
Citizen Engagement: Innovation matching grant beneficiary annual survey (number of surveys)

comment.narrative: <p>Engagement Survey is mainstreamed in IF activities, and the fourth survey was conducted in January 2021. In addition to the Survey, the IF conducted other Citizen Engagement activities, which are now fully integrated in their work program. This includes regular Open Door Days events running for several weeks after the announcement of a call for proposals, where all interested parties can come and get advice and guidance from the IF about the programs. It also includes having email and phone lines to respond to any queries potential applicants might have. Also, the IF occasionally organizes workshops, both for potential applicants and for awardees. These activities have been impacted by COVID-19 crisis with many of the consultations moving on-line, but once the situation improves it is planned that these activities will return to the more traditional format.</p>

title.narrative: Citizen engagement: Number of employers reached by client satisfaction and needs survey

comment.narrative: <p>Surveys of employers, and citizen engagement activities more broadly, were impacted by the COVID-19 crisis and where thus significantly lower than originally planned. Nevertheless, NES plans to ramp up these activities once epidemic situation stabilizes. In addition, prior to the COVID-19 crisis NES was performing other citizen engagement activities. For example in 2019 about 70 job fairs have been organized across the country, with over 50,000 unemployed and about 1,000 employers attending. Also, NES is conducting regular field visits to employers (see indicator above). Finally, NES is also partnering up with the Chamber of Commerce for a survey of employers and employees, with original plans to implement it in Q1 2021, though this has been delayed due to unfavorable epidemic situation. Once COVID-19 crisis has subsided, the NES plans to resume with these various citizen engagement services.</p>

NES registered unemployment cases transitioning into formal job (annual)

comment.narrative:
<p>The number of registered unemployed transitioning into a formal job in 2019 and 2020 is decreasing, but this reflects positive developments. Namely, there was a decrease in the total number of registered unemployed as a result of the improving labor market conditions. Number of unemployed decreased both in 2018 and 2019, and has remained at this lower level in 2020. Thus, the pool of
 unemployed is now lower by about 200,000 compared to baseline 2014. As a result, due to this exogenous factor and smaller pool of unemployed, the absolute number of those transitioning to formal work is lower. However, as a percentage of unemployed, transition to formal employment is consistently increasing - from about 33 percent of unemployed in 2015 to over 50 percent in the more recent data. Further, for 2020 the number of unemployed transitioning into a formal job has been significantly impacted by the COVID-19
 pandemic crisis.</p>

Number of firms participating in the new Supplier Development Program

comment.narrative: <p>Total of 32 firms participated in the program so far. This includes 19 from the first program call in 2019, and an additional 13from the second call in 2020. Implementation of the Supplier Development Program has been significantly impacted due to COVID-19 pandemic, since decisions on program participation involve physical visits to facilities of potential participants to perform diagnostics. In 2020, SDA has started implementing tools to conduct remote diagnostics, but this has only partially mitigated the issues caused by the pandemic. As a result, number of firms participating in 2020 is lower than in 2019.</p>
<p>This indicator was introduced during the first restructuring of the project.</p>

title.narrative: Science Fund programs competitive grants awarded

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was introduced during the first restructuring of the project. The actual value of the indicator includes the number of approved projects under three programs where evaluations have been completed and grants awarded (PROMIS: 59 projects, AI program: 12 projects, Covid-19 special program: 14 projects). Evaluation of the project proposals for the fourth program (IDEAS) was underway at project completion, and it was anticipated that a further 80-150 grants would be awarded under this program. Finally, additional 92 grant awards have been approved for the DIASPORA program.</p>
